newsitem.title: FRANCE: Durum yields seen down 26 percent in Midi-Pyrenees.
newsitem.headline: Durum yields seen down 26 percent in Midi-Pyrenees.

text.p: Durum yields in the Midi-Pyrenees region, France's second producing zone for the pasta-making grain, are set to fall around 26 percent this year due to drought, according to latest official estimates from the region.
Crop officials based in Toulouse, the region's capital, said on Wednesday they predicted an average regional yield of four tonnes per hectare, down 26 percent from 5.42 tonnes last year.
But the estimates are provisional and the risk is more on the downside as analysts revise their figures when the harvest comes in, they said.
The area sown locally to durum was basically stable this year at 69,000 hectares, compared with 69,200 last year, national cereals office ONIC said earlier this month.
The yield loss is almost entirely the result of four months without rain between January and April, although a cold snap in late spring also did some damage, officials said.
The harvest is ready to start but has been delayed by rain in the past few days -- far too late to help the grain which is already ripe.

The current yield estimate of four tonnes per hectare -- slightly lower at 3.8 or 3.9 tonnes per hectare, according to one official crop analyst -- would imply regional production of 276,000 tonnes, also down 26 percent from last year's 375,000.

Quality is not seen as a major problem this year, however, with the lack of rain discouraging disease and also secondary shoots -- tillering -- in the plant. This has the advantage of trapping what nourishment the plant gets from the soil in a smaller number of wheat ears, analysts said.
"Disease outbreaks are not exceptional this year, I would say within the norm. Where the soil was least affected by drought the situation is quite good," one official said.
ONIC figures averaged by Reuters show that the region's five-year durum yield for 1992-1996 was 4.51 tonnes a hectare.
The region's 1997 durum sowings account for 27 percent of the country's total durum area of 256,840 hectares.
